title: Split Lighting
description: Split lighting divides the face into a lit half and a shadow half by placing the key at about 90 degrees to the nose, a vertical cut down the center line. There is no Rembrandt triangle and no loop; the far plane is largely gone.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Duality made as geometry: hero and liar, cop and crook, the same person cut in two. The audience gets one eye in light and one in almost nothing.
Music, crime, and moral argument use it because the cut is literal. It is the wrong tool for charm, romance, or any beat that needs both cheeks.
If you sneak fill across the center line, the split collapses into side lighting with wrap. If you raise the key and pull it forward, you may accidentally make Rembrandt.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Put a relatively hard key at 90 degrees to the face, at about eye height, so the shadow edge runs down forehead, nose, and chin. Fill is near zero.
Color can be a hard white or a theatrical gel; the point is the cut, not prettiness. A true split is more severe than generic side light because the wrap over the nose is killed with flags if needed.
Prompt: Split lighting on [Subject], one half of the face in light, the other in shadow, a vertical moral cut.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when a character is two things at once, a drummer under a side spot, a don in profile thought. Do not use it on a first-date close-up unless you want threat.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Side lighting is the broader 90-degree direction and can still wrap a body or a room. Split is the facial pattern with a hard center line.
Rembrandt lighting keeps a triangle on the dark cheek; split does not. Loop lighting is much more frontal.
Short lighting can include a split if the dark cheek faces camera, but short is about which cheek the camera sees, not the 90-degree cut. Butterfly is the opposite: both cheeks open.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The Godfather uses half-lit faces in the office so thought reads as a cut. Whiplash slashes players with hard side spots that often split the face on stage.
The pattern is the center line, not a mood word.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Rembrandt or wrapped side lighting. The tell is a pocket of light on the dark cheek, or a soft wrap over the nose.
Fix it by moving the key to 90 degrees and killing fill until the center line is clean.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is split lighting in film?
A key at about 90 degrees that lights one half of the face and leaves the other in shadow. The cut runs vertically down the center of the face.
Split lighting vs Rembrandt lighting
Split has no triangle on the dark cheek; that half is gone. Rembrandt keeps a small triangle of light under the shadow-side eye.
When should I use split lighting?
Use it for duality, interrogation, or a theatrical side spot. Skip it when both eyes and both cheeks must sell a line.
How do I prompt split lighting for AI image or video?
Place the key at 90 degrees. State one half of the face in light, the other in shadow, no fill, no Rembrandt triangle.
